context: Interactive 3D WebGL scatter plot of 1500 named CSS colors positioned in OKLCH color space (Hue→X, Lightness→Y, Chroma→Z) with orbit camera, lightness/chroma slice-plane range sliders, and hover tooltips showing color name and OKLCH values.
first_impression: The self-coloring point cloud immediately reads as a color gamut volume — each dot encodes its own identity, eliminating any legend-lookup burden.
what_works: Self-encoding colors remove all working-memory cost for category matching; slice-plane controls reduce 1500-point density to inspectable subsets on demand, making the interaction genuinely useful for exploration rather than decorative.
what_doesnt: No 3D axis guides or grid planes make it impossible to read precise OKLCH coordinates from position alone — the bottom text label is too abstract without visual anchors in the scene. Auto-rotation (active when not dragging) prevents a stable reference frame, so viewers cannot reliably compare point positions across interactions without first stopping the rotation.
